analysis:
The supplied PR change is documentation-only: CHANGELOG.md was modified in two head_text units (7e16eb3337db8652:8 and :9). No source code, configuration, or threat-model files are shown, so I could not verify any of the described behavior and found no concrete security regression in the visible text.

Several changelog entries describe security-relevant behavior that sits in unchanged or unsupplied source. Later passes should check that source against these threat IDs and boundaries:

- Demanded prefix reuse and SSD write-share changes. These bear on T-041 and SEC-035 (cross-tenant prefix-cache sharing and the TTFT oracle). Specifically, authenticated repeated checkpoints now get access to the reserved SSD write share on first local appearance. This should not weaken the HMAC-keyed lookup tags, the 30-minute TTL, per-account salt scoping, or the disk budget. The write-budget raise from 150 to 750 GB/day is relevant to SSD wear and disk-use policy. Also confirm that the 'COMPLETE donation hashing bounded by the checkpoint' change keeps the authenticated address and cacheSalt folding intact.
- Cache-routing persistence and holder restore. This touches the TB-001 and TB-002 routing state and the cache_route_keys.go scope derivation. The entry says no prompts or raw chain hashes are persisted. The changelog's claim that persisted holders bind only to matching live provider capabilities is not verifiable here.
- Provider 0.9.17 and Autopilot changes. These affect the TB-002/TB-011 serving authorization and model-loading boundaries. Check that the live lease is required before additional models become loadable.
- Autopilot unload-victim validation and the bank payout migration. The payout migration covers Stripe webhook verification and atomic settlement for TB-008, T-030, and A-009. Verify that the legacy Connect webhook secrets are separate and that duplicate-credit handling is atomic.
- Coordinator legacy-compat cleanup. The changelog claims removal of the unauthenticated wallet earnings endpoint, which resolves T-031. The threat model's T-031 entry may need its status refreshed. It also claims attestation challenges now fail closed, App Attest protocol 3 only, and a routing floor on MIN_PROVIDER_VERSION. These relate to T-033, T-036, T-052..T-058 and TB-009/TB-011.
- Coordinator-side changes in the 0.9.10 and 0.9.11 sections. These cover App Attest rotation limits and diagnostics, public model-demand aggregates with k-anonymity suppression (cohorts under 20 requests or 3 accounts), and the diagnostics/archive privacy of T-058. Verify the suppression thresholds and the claim that hidden counts cannot be recovered by subtraction.
- The 'advisory threat-model review' entries. Check that the workflow executes only trusted base-revision code and handles untrusted PR text safely.

No findings are filed for the visible text. Because changelog prose cannot show the code behavior, I am not claiming any of it is safe.
